title: 458. Helen of Troy: A Family of Blood (Part 2)

sentences.en: If only he hadn't taken it into his head to dig in a sleepy backwater village for Troy's walls and somehow found them.
sentences.zh: 要不是他突发奇想，在一个沉睡的偏远村庄里挖掘特洛伊的城墙，并且阴差阳错地找到了它们，那就好了。

sentences.en: If he hadn't knelt in the dirt all day with beautiful Sophia chipping away crust from the tiles of Priam's palace.
sentences.zh: 要不是他整天跪在泥土里，和美丽的索菲亚一起凿开普里阿摩斯王宫地砖上的硬壳，那就好了。

sentences.en: From bracelets that had once circled the slim wrists of princesses.
sentences.zh: 从曾经环绕着公主纤细手腕的手镯开始。

sentences.en: If he hadn't proven that his dream was graspable, that the stories he loved were fashioned in the high style, not to escape the world, but to remember it.
sentences.zh: 要不是他证明了自己的梦想是可以触及的，他所热爱的那些故事有着崇高的风格，不是为了逃避现实，而是为了铭记现实。

sentences.en: A tribute to the dead, to the dead bright ones whose gestures, vivid as they are in song, were doubtless in the flesh more dazzling.
sentences.zh: 这是对死者的致敬，是对那些耀眼死者的致敬——他们在歌谣中的姿态虽然生动，但在血肉之躯时无疑更加耀眼夺目。

sentences.en: So that was a poem about Heinrich Schliemann by the American poet Carl Davis.
sentences.zh: 所以，那是美国诗人卡尔·戴维斯写的一首关于海因里希·施利曼的诗。

sentences.en: And right there, Tom, you have this sort of sense of the dead bright ones, more dazzling, more terrifying in the flesh than they were in reality.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，就在那里，你会有这样一种感觉：那些耀眼的死者，在现实的血肉之躯中比在虚构中更加耀眼，也更加令人敬畏。

sentences.en: And as that poem suggests, Schliemann's great fame, we ended the last episode by talking about this German archaeologist who is famous for having, in inverted commas,
sentences.zh: 正如那首诗所暗示的那样，施利曼享有盛名——我们在上一集的结尾讨论过这位德国考古学家，他以“发现”了特洛伊而闻名，

sentences.en: discovered Troy.
sentences.zh: 发现特洛伊。

sentences.en: His fame is bound up with the idea, isn't it, that the stories we talked about last time are true.
sentences.zh: 他的名气与这样一个观念息息相关，不是吗：我们上期谈论的那些故事都是真的。

sentences.en: That there was a Trojan war, that there might have even been a wooden horse, that there was a Helen of Troy.
sentences.zh: 真的有过特洛伊战争，甚至可能真的有过木马，真的有特洛伊的海伦。

sentences.en: So we teased this at the end of the last episode.
sentences.zh: 所以在上一集的末尾，我们卖了个关子。

sentences.en: Let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Who is Heinrich Schliemann, probably the most famous archaeologist who ever lived?
sentences.zh: 海因里希·施利曼究竟是谁？他或许是有史以来最著名的考古学家。

sentences.en: So Schliemann, he was the son of a Lutheran pastor who got caught up in a sex scandal.
sentences.zh: 施利曼是一个路德教牧师的儿子，他的父亲卷入了一场性丑闻。

sentences.en: Oh no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不会吧。

sentences.en: And so the young Heinrich was kind of impoverished and humiliated, but discovered that he had an incredible aptitude for languages and ended up a fabulously wealthy businessman.
sentences.zh: 因此，年轻的海因里希一度陷入贫困和屈辱，但他发现自己极具语言天赋，最终成了一名富可敌国的商人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He is a product of Germany at its most expansionist, self-confident, but also kind of insecure.
sentences.zh: 他是德国处于最具扩张性、最自信但也带有某种不安全感时期的产物。

sentences.en: He's a fascinating figure.
sentences.zh: 他是一个迷人的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Schliemann would later claim that back when he was a child in Mecklenburg in East Germany, Dominic, he had been reading about Troy and Helen as a seven-year-old.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，施利曼后来声称，早在他在德国东部梅克伦堡度过童年时，他七岁的时候就在读关于特洛伊和海伦的故事了。

sentences.en: This is probably not true.
sentences.zh: 这大概不是真的。

sentences.en: Schliemann is brilliant at creating his own mythology, ironically enough.
sentences.zh: 说来讽刺，施利曼非常擅长创造自己的神话。

sentences.en: He's a kind of great monstrous figure of high achievement, high ambition, kind of almost Wagnerian character.
sentences.zh: 他是一个拥有伟大成就和宏大野心的庞大怪物般的人物，几乎带有瓦格纳式的性格色彩。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or maybe even the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至像德皇。

sentences.en: Oh no, I can't believe you're bad-mouthing the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 噢不，我真不敢相信你在说德皇的坏话。

sentences.en: But he's not always 100% truthful.
sentences.zh: 但他并不总是百分之百说实话。

sentences.en: And Helen is a kind of obsession for him.
sentences.zh: 海伦对他来说是一种近乎执念的存在。

sentences.en: And just as the Greek heroes go and search for Helen, so does Schliemann.
sentences.zh: 正如希腊英雄们去寻找海伦一样，施利曼也是如此。

sentences.en: And this obsession is so great that in 1869, he's been married to a Russian woman.
sentences.zh: 这种执念如此之深，以至于在1869年，当时他已经娶了一位俄罗斯妻子。

sentences.en: Russian was one of his many languages and he'd been working in St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 俄语是他的众多语言之一，他之前一直在圣彼得堡工作。

sentences.en: He divorces her and he decides that he'd like a real-life Helen to replace her.
sentences.zh: 他与她离婚，并决定找一个现实生活中的海伦来取代她。

sentences.en: And so amazingly, he employs a Greek archbishop basically to pimp him, you know, a suitable Helen.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，他雇了一个希腊大主教来为他物色一个合适的海伦。

sentences.en: And the archbishop finds one in the form of a 16-year-old Greek girl who's called Sophia, who is the Sophia that was name-checked in that poem that you read.
sentences.zh: 大主教帮他找到了一个16岁的希腊女孩，名叫索菲亚，她就是你刚才读的那首诗中提到的索菲亚。

sentences.en: And Schliemann has specified that she has to be poor and she has to be educated.
sentences.zh: 施利曼特别规定，她必须出身贫寒且受过教育。

sentences.en: And so he interviews her and asks her to recite Homer and Sophia does.
sentences.zh: 于是他面试了她，让她背诵荷马史诗，索菲亚照做了。

sentences.en: And so the marriage goes ahead.
sentences.zh: 于是这桩婚事就这么定下来了。

sentences.en: So he has his own Helen in the form of Sophia.
sentences.zh: 就这样，他找到了以索菲亚为化身的海伦。

sentences.en: The following year in 1870, he goes to the northwestern corner of what is now Turkey, where tradition placed the site of Troy.
sentences.zh: 第二年，即1870年，他来到了现今土耳其的西北角，传统上认为特洛伊的遗址就在那里。

sentences.en: Troy, and he starts excavating a hill called Hissalik.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊，他开始在一座名为希萨里克的小山丘上进行发掘。

sentences.en: And he's there for two years.
sentences.zh: 他在那里待了两年。

sentences.en: And in 1872, he announces that he has found a burnt city, which he identifies with the very Troy burnt by the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 1872年，他宣布自己发现了一座被大火焚毁的城市，他将其认定为被希腊人付之一炬的特洛伊城。

sentences.en: And then the following year in May, he finds a spectacular hoard of gold and silver.
sentences.zh: 紧接着在第二年的五月，他发现了一批惊人的金银财宝。

sentences.en: And among this hoard, there's a great collection of jewelry, which he calls inevitably the Jewels of Helen.
sentences.zh: 在这批宝藏中，有大量精美的珠宝，他无可避免地将其命名为“海伦的珠宝”。

sentences.en: And Schliemann tells a story about how Sophia had been with him, how she had carried the jewels from the site where they'd found them in her skirts.
sentences.zh: 施利曼讲述了一个故事：索菲亚当时和他在一起，她用裙子将珠宝从发现的遗址中运了出去。

sentences.en: This is, again, not true.
sentences.zh: 这也是假的。

sentences.en: Sophia had been in Athens at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时索菲亚根本不在场，而在雅典。

sentences.en: But what Schliemann then does is to dress her up in the jewels and to say that he has found the treasure of Priam, the king of Troy.
sentences.zh: 但施利曼接下来做的是，让索菲亚盛装打扮并戴上这些珠宝，声称自己找到了特洛伊国王普里阿摩斯的宝藏。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是神来之笔。

sentences.en: He seems to have discovered Helen of Troy.
sentences.zh: 他似乎真的发现了特洛伊的海伦。

sentences.en: Now, Helen, of course, was only one of two sisters who were hatched by Leda, their mother.
sentences.zh: 当然，海伦其实是勒达这位母亲所生的一对孪生姐妹之一。

sentences.en: So we talked about this, Dominic, in the previous episode, how Leda was raped by Zeus in the form of a giant swan
sentences.zh: 所以我们在上一集里谈到过，多米尼克，勒达是如何被化身为巨天鹅的宙斯强暴的，

sentences.en: and gave birth to Helen, who was Zeus's daughter, and gave birth to Clytemnestra, who was the daughter of Leda's mortal husband, Tindareus, the king of Sparta.
sentences.zh: 并生下了宙斯的女儿海伦，以及勒达的凡人丈夫、斯巴达国王廷达瑞俄斯的女儿克吕泰涅斯特拉。

sentences.en: And we talked as well about how Clytemnestra married the elder brother of Menelaus, who was called Agamemnon.
sentences.zh: 我们还谈到过克吕泰涅斯特拉是如何嫁给墨涅拉俄斯的哥哥阿伽门农的。

sentences.en: And Agamemnon is the king of a Greek city called Mycenae, where Clytemnestra rules as the queen.
sentences.zh: 阿伽门农是一座名为迈锡尼的希腊城市的国王，克吕泰涅斯特拉在那里作为王后统治着。

sentences.en: And so Schliemann, having, in his opinion, discovered Troy, discovered the jewels of Helen, having proven that Helen had actually existed,
sentences.zh: 因此，施利曼在自认为发现了特洛伊、发现了海伦的珠宝、证明了海伦真实存在之后，

sentences.en: the obvious target for his next excavation would be Mycenae, the city ruled by Agamemnon, where Helen's sister, Clytemnestra, was queen.
sentences.zh: 他的下一个发掘目标自然而然就是迈锡尼——这座由阿伽门农统治、海伦的姐姐克吕泰涅斯特拉担任王后的城市。

sentences.en: And so that's what he decides to do.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定这么做。

sentences.en: There's a problem with this because, you know, Greece is now an independent state.
sentences.zh: 这中间有个问题，因为当时的希腊已经是一个独立国家了。

sentences.en: So it's not kind of Lord Elgin conditions where he could just turn up and do it.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像埃尔金勋爵时期那样，他可以随便出现就能开挖。

sentences.en: So in 1874, he heads to the Peloponnese, which is the southern bit of Greece.
sentences.zh: 于是在1874年，他前往伯罗奔尼撒半岛，也就是希腊南部。

sentences.en: Yeah, the southern peninsula.
sentences.zh: 对，南部的那个半岛。

sentences.en: And he heads to Mycenae, which is kind of in the northeast corner of it, kind of set among mountains.
sentences.zh: 他前往迈锡尼，它大概位于半岛的东北角，坐落于群山之中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he starts this completely illegal dig, and the Greeks close it down.
sentences.zh: 他开始了一场完全非法的挖掘，结果被希腊人叫停了。

sentences.en: So Schliemann gets around this problem by giving a massive bung to the Greek Archaeological Society, who then decide, yeah, that's great, you can go ahead.
sentences.zh: 于是施利曼通过向希腊考古学会行贿巨款解决了这个问题，学会随后决定：行，这太棒了，你可以继续挖了。

sentences.en: And so he starts excavating in this site.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始在这个遗址进行发掘。

sentences.en: And I think there's no question that just as at Troy, he was looking for Helen.
sentences.zh: 我认为毫无疑问，就像在特洛伊时他寻找海伦一样。

sentences.en: So in a sense, at Mycenae, Schliemann is looking for certainly Agamemnon, the king there, but also his wife, Clytemnestra.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，在迈锡尼，施利曼寻找的不仅是那里的国王阿伽门农，还有他的妻子克吕泰涅斯特拉。

sentences.en: Because although Clytemnestra is not as celebrated as Helen, she too, like Helen, is a figure of incredible potency in Greek mythology, and particularly in tragic literature.
sentences.zh: 因为尽管克吕泰涅斯特拉不如海伦那么出名，但她和海伦一样，在希腊神话中也是一个极具爆发力的人物，特别是在悲剧文学中。

sentences.en: Bloodstained figure, Tom.
sentences.zh: 一个满手血腥的人物，汤姆。

sentences.en: Bloodstained figure, yeah.
sentences.zh: 满手血腥的人物，是的。

sentences.en: So although Clytemnestra is not as celebrated as Helen of Troy, I mean, she is a significant figure in Greek mythology,
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管克吕泰涅斯特拉不如特洛伊的海伦那么著名，我的意思是，她仍然是希腊神话中的一个重要人物，
zh_words: 泰涅斯特拉不如特洛伊

sentences.en: and particularly in the literature of democratic Athens in its 5th century BC heyday.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在公元前5世纪雅典民主鼎盛时期的文学作品中。

sentences.en: And she is the dominant figure in one of the supreme literary achievements of ancient Athens, which is a series of three plays by a tragedian called Aeschylus.
sentences.zh: 她是一部古雅典文学巅峰之作中的核心人物，那是由悲剧作家埃斯库罗斯创作的三部曲。

sentences.en: Aeschylus was a veteran of the Persian Wars.
sentences.zh: 埃斯库罗斯是波斯战争的老兵。

sentences.en: He'd fought at Marathon.
sentences.zh: 他参加过马拉松战役。

sentences.en: He'd fought at Salamis.
sentences.zh: 他参加过萨拉米斯战役。

sentences.en: Every year he would enter a play for the annual contest that the Athenians staged in honour of Dionysus, and he would always win.
sentences.zh: 每年他都会带着一部剧作参加雅典人为纪念狄奥尼索斯而举办的年度戏剧比赛，而且他总是能赢。

sentences.en: And eventually he got killed, according to tradition.
sentences.zh: 根据传说，他最终死于一次意外。

sentences.en: He was very bald.
sentences.zh: 他是个极度谢顶的人。

sentences.en: And an eagle is supposed to have dropped a tortoise on his head, mistaking his head for a stone.
sentences.zh: 据说有一只老鹰误把他的光头当成了石头，从空中扔下了一只乌龟砸中了他的头。

sentences.en: I don't know, why would that kill you more likely if you were bald than if you had a normal head of hair?
sentences.zh: 我不明白，为什么如果你秃顶的话，这比你有一头浓密的头发更容易要你的命？

sentences.en: Because the eagle thought that his bald head was a stone.
sentences.zh: 因为老鹰把他的光头当成石头了。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 那也算合理。

sentences.en: So, yeah, just tipping you off there to beware of eagles carrying tortoises, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，多米尼克，我只是提醒你要小心那些带着乌龟的老鹰。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你。

sentences.en: And he's commemorated as one of the giant figures of classical Athens.
sentences.zh: 他被人们当作古典雅典的伟大巨人之一来缅怀。

sentences.en: And the play that describes Clytemnestra's relationship with Agamemnon in the most detail, and it has to be said the most bloody detail, was called the Agamemnon.
sentences.zh: 那部以最详细、而且必须承认是最血腥的笔触来描述克吕泰涅斯特拉与阿伽门农关系的戏剧，名字就叫《阿伽门农》。

sentences.en: And it was part of this trilogy, as I said, that in 458 BC won the top prize.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，它是这座三部曲的一部分，该剧于公元前458年荣获最高奖项。

sentences.en: And just as Homer, when he introduces Helen, takes for granted that people will know who Helen is.
sentences.zh: 正如荷马在引入海伦时，理所当然地认为人们会知道海伦是谁一样。

sentences.en: So to a degree, Aeschylus is able to take for granted that people will know who Clytemnestra is, and who Agamemnon is, and what the backdrop to their story is.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，埃斯库罗斯也可以理所当然地认为，人们会知道克吕泰涅斯特拉是谁，阿伽门农是谁，以及他们故事的背景是什么。

sentences.en: So I think before we continue with our account of what Schliemann finds in Mycenae,
sentences.zh: 所以我想在我们继续讲述施利曼在迈锡尼的发现之前，

sentences.en: we should perhaps just go into the details of who Clytemnestra is and what the family is that she's married into.
sentences.zh: 我们或许应该先深入探讨一下克吕泰涅斯特拉是谁，以及她嫁入的是一个怎样的家族。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好极了。

sentences.en: Because it has to be said, it is probably the most nightmarish collection of in-laws that anyone could possibly have.
sentences.zh: 因为必须承认，这可能是任何人所能遇到的最像噩梦的一堆姻亲了。

sentences.en: So Tom, who are Agamemnon's forebears?
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，阿伽门农的祖先都有谁？

sentences.en: So Agamemnon's great-grandfather is a guy called Tantalus, who is the son of Zeus, and he hosts the gods for a great banquet.
sentences.zh: 阿伽门农的曾祖父是一个叫坦塔罗斯的人，他是宙斯的儿子，他曾举办了一场盛宴款待众神。

sentences.en: And basically, just for the bants, he cooks his son, a boy called Pelops, and serves him up in the banquet to see whether the gods will be able to tell his trick.
sentences.zh: 基本上，纯粹是为了好玩，他把自己的儿子——一个叫珀洛普斯的男孩——给煮了，并做成菜端上宴席，看看众神能不能识破他的把戏。

sentences.en: And the gods all do find this, but one of them, Demeter, because she's lost her daughter, Persephone, to the god of the underworld, is very depressed.
sentences.zh: 众神一眼就看穿了，但其中一位女神德墨忒尔，因为女儿珀耳塞福涅被冥王夺走而情绪非常低落。

sentences.en: So she nibbles on the feast and eats Pelops' shoulder.
sentences.zh: 所以她心不在焉地吃了一口，吃掉了珀洛普斯的一只肩膀。

sentences.en: And the gods are incredibly angry.
sentences.zh: 众神勃然大怒。

sentences.en: They bring Pelops back to life.
sentences.zh: 他们让珀洛普斯复活了。

sentences.en: They give him a shoulder made of ivory, and they put Tantalus in the depths of hell.
sentences.zh: 他们用象牙给他做一个肩膀，并把坦塔罗斯打入地狱深处。

sentences.en: Right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: Where he's surrounded by water, which he can't drink, and by grapes, which are always out of reach.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他被水环绕却无法饮用，周围挂着葡萄却永远够不着。

sentences.en: He's being tantalized, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他被“折磨”了，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's tantalized.
sentences.zh: 是的，他饱受折磨。

sentences.en: Pelops, his son, we've actually already mentioned him.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子珀洛普斯，我们其实已经提到过他了。

sentences.en: He's the guy who founds the Olympic Games, and he gives his name to the Peloponnese, the island of Pelops.
sentences.zh: 他就是创立奥林匹克运动会的人，伯罗奔尼撒半岛（意为“珀洛普斯之岛”）就是以他的名字命名的。

sentences.zh: 所以，迈锡尼和特洛伊有所不同。

sentences.en: Troy had been forgotten about.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊曾被人遗忘。

sentences.en: Nobody knew where it was.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道它在哪里。

sentences.en: People always knew where Mycenae was.
sentences.zh: 但人们一直都知道迈锡尼在哪里。

sentences.en: And people had already begun excavating there.
sentences.zh: 而且人们已经在那里开始了考古发掘。

sentences.en: So as early as 1700, a Venetian engineer had gone and he had removed all the kind of debris that had slid down the mountain and buried Mycenae.
sentences.zh: 早在1700年，就有一位威尼斯工程师去过那里，并清理了所有从山上滑落并埋没迈锡尼的碎石泥土。

sentences.en: And actually, Lord Elgin had gone there.
sentences.zh: 实际上，埃尔金勋爵也去过那里。

sentences.en: So the gateway into Mycenae, it's called the Lion Gate.
sentences.zh: 迈锡尼的入口被称为狮子门。

sentences.en: It has two images of lions over it.
sentences.zh: 它的上方雕刻着两尊狮子的雕像。

sentences.en: Although actually, they're not lions, they're lionesses, which is appropriate, bearing in mind that it was the home of Clytemnestra.
sentences.zh: 尽管实际上它们不是狮子，而是母狮，考虑到这里曾是克吕泰涅斯特拉的故居，这也算很贴切。

sentences.en: And he wanted to take that back to the British Museum as well.
sentences.zh: 他也想把这个运回大英博物馆。

sentences.en: But he couldn't because it is enormous.
sentences.zh: 但他做不到，因为它太巨大了。

sentences.en: Mycenae is built out of the most enormous stones.
sentences.zh: 迈锡尼是用极其巨大的石头建造的。

sentences.en: And so even the Greeks were impressed.
sentences.zh: 因此，连古希腊人都为之震撼。

sentences.en: They called it Cyclopean.
sentences.zh: 他们将其称为“巨石文明”式的（Cyclopean）。

sentences.en: Cyclopes are kind of giant one-eyed monsters who were supposed to have built it.
sentences.zh: 独眼巨人是传说中建造了这一切的独眼巨怪。

sentences.en: So it's not as though Schliemann is dealing archaeologically with entirely virgin territory when he starts digging there in 1876.
sentences.zh: 所以，当施里曼在1876年开始在那里挖掘时，并不意味着他在考古学上面对的是一片完全未开发的处女地。

sentences.en: But he does have a nose for the incredible find.
sentences.zh: 但他确实有着对惊人发现的敏锐直觉。

sentences.en: And what he's done is that kind of just to the right of the Lion Gate, inside the great walls of Mycenae, he's found a circle of stone slabs.
sentences.zh: 他所做的是，在狮子门的右侧、迈锡尼宏伟的城墙内部，发现了一个由石板围成的圆圈。

sentences.en: And within it, there's a kind of series of weird, upright stones.
sentences.zh: 在它内部，有一系列奇怪的、竖立着的石头。

sentences.en: And some of these have relief sculptures.
sentences.zh: 其中一些石头上还刻有浮雕。

sentences.en: And Schliemann, the moment he finds these, he says, brilliant, I found the tombs of Agamemnon and Cassandra.
sentences.zh: 施里曼一发现这些，就说：“太棒了，我找到了阿伽门农和卡珊德拉的陵墓。”

sentences.en: So he's immediately identifying his archaeological finds with the stories that he's read in Aeschylus and so on.
sentences.zh: 因此，他立刻将自己的考古发现与他在埃斯库罗斯等人的作品中读到的故事联系在了一起。

sentences.en: But even better, he finds these very, very kind of deep shaft graves beneath the tombstones.
sentences.zh: 但更棒的是，他在墓碑下方发现了非常非常深的竖穴墓。

sentences.en: And he excavates these.
sentences.zh: 他对这些墓穴进行了发掘。

sentences.en: And in each of these tombs, he finds bodies.
sentences.zh: 他在每一座陵墓里都发现了遗体。

sentences.en: Sometimes he finds treasure.
sentences.zh: 有时他能发现宝藏。

sentences.en: He finds all kinds of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他发现了各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: And some of the bodies are wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 其中一些遗体还戴着面具。

sentences.en: And it's in the final shaft that he finds the famous mask, the one of gold, which is always called the face of Agamemnon.
sentences.zh: 正是在最后一个竖穴墓里，他发现了那张著名的黄金面具，也就是一直被称为“阿伽门农的面脸”的那张。

sentences.en: But the thing is that this isn't actually what Schliemann meant by the face of Agamemnon.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这其实并不是施里曼所说的“阿伽门农的脸”。

sentences.en: When he lifted the mask, the face beneath it crumbled.
sentences.zh: 当他揭开面具时，底下的脸瞬间化为了灰烬。

sentences.en: So he never actually, you know, he didn't know what that face looked like.
sentences.zh: 所以他其实从未真正……你知道的，他根本不知道那张脸长什么样。

sentences.en: But there was another one in another tomb.
sentences.zh: 但另一座墓里还有另一个。

sentences.en: So when he was talking about the face of Agamemnon, what he actually was referring to was not the mask, but to a head that had survived, a kind of skull that had survived.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他谈到阿伽门农的脸时，他实际指的其实不是面具，而是一个保存下来的头部，一个保存下来的头骨。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he did a drawing of it.
sentences.zh: 而且他还为此画了一张素描。

sentences.en: And it appeared in the book that he published about his excavations at Mycenae.
sentences.zh: 这张图发表在他出版的关于迈锡尼发掘工作的书中。

sentences.en: And it looks like E.T.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像外星人E.T.

sentences.en: That's 3,000 years old, right?
sentences.zh: 那可是有三千年历史了吧？

sentences.en: Or whatever, however many thousand years old.
sentences.zh: 或者随便多少千年历史。

sentences.en: How old is it?
sentences.zh: 它到底有多久远？

sentences.en: Well, it's actually older than Schliemann thought, because Schliemann thought that it was dated to around 1250 BC, which is the date of the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 好吧，它实际上比施里曼想象的还要古老，因为施里曼认为它的年代大约在公元前1250年，也就是特洛伊战争的时期。

sentences.en: But it's actually about 400 years older than that.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上比那个时期还要早大约400年。

sentences.en: So even if Agamemnon had existed, it wasn't Agamemnon.
sentences.zh: 所以，即便阿伽门农真的存在过，那也不是阿伽门农。

sentences.en: And this gets discovered in the wake of Schliemann's finds, because basically in the wake of Schliemann, archaeology begins to kind of professionalize itself.
sentences.zh: 这一发现在施里曼的发现之后大白于天下，因为基本上在施里曼之后，考古学开始走向专业化。

sentences.en: And over the course of the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪期间，

sentences.en: kind of academic archaeologists come to feel really embarrassed about the idea that you're going to these places to look for legendary figures.
sentences.zh: 学术界的考古学家们开始对那种“去这些地方寻找传说中人物”的想法感到非常尴尬。

sentences.en: It's a bit like archaeologists going to Palestine, start to feel a bit embarrassed about the idea that they're looking for biblical sites.
sentences.zh: 这有点像考古学家去巴勒斯坦时，开始对寻找圣经遗址的想法感到有些尴尬一样。

sentences.en: Or if you ask an archaeologist about King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你去问考古学家关于亚瑟王的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, they kind of, they sigh and they look very miserable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们往往会叹气，看起来非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And you're trying to make it too interesting.
sentences.zh: 而你却试图把它变得太有趣了。

sentences.en: You're having too much fun.
sentences.zh: 你玩得太开心了。

sentences.en: And they want to suck the life out of it.
sentences.zh: 而他们却想榨干其中的生机。

sentences.en: But also, of course, in the wake of the Second World War, there are further reasons,
sentences.zh: 但当然，在第二次世界大战之后，还有其他原因，

sentences.en: which is that, you know, the emphasis on Helen being white and golden-haired and Agamemnon as a great ruler of men.
sentences.zh: 那就是，你知道，强调海伦是白皮肤、金头发，以及阿伽门农作为伟大的统治者。

sentences.en: This had been very strongly eulogized by Nazis, among others.
sentences.zh: 这一点曾被纳粹等极力赞美。

sentences.en: Of course, I forgot.
sentences.zh: 当然，我差点忘了。

sentences.en: The Nazis thought that the ancient Greeks were good Aryans, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 纳粹认为古希腊人是优秀的雅利安人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So there was a definite sense that kind of looking for these legendary figures of Greek myth was kind of incipiently Nazi.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种明确的感觉，即寻找希腊神话中的这些传奇人物带有某种纳粹的萌芽。

sentences.en: And also, the other thing that happens is that the language used by the Mycenaeans, what's called Linear B, gets cracked.
sentences.zh: 还有，发生另一件事是，迈锡尼人使用的语言，也就是所谓的线性文字B，被破解了。

sentences.en: And people can start reading what is on all the kind of burnt tablets that have been found at various cities like Mycenae across Greece.
sentences.zh: 人们开始能够阅读在希腊各地如迈锡尼等不同城市发现的所有烧焦的泥板上的内容。

sentences.en: And it opens up a world not of Homeric warriors, but of bureaucrats.
sentences.zh: 它开启的不是一个荷马笔下的勇士世界，而是一个官僚的世界。

sentences.en: And you get records of kind of farmers and potters and weavers and so on.
sentences.zh: 你会看到关于农民、陶工、织工等各种记录。

sentences.en: And there's nothing about golden-haired warriors and chariots or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 里面没有任何关于金发勇士、战车之类的内容。

sentences.en: And this contributes to a sense after the Second World War that it's somehow politically the wrong thing to do,
sentences.zh: 这促成了二战后的一种感觉，即从政治上讲，这样做是不对的，

sentences.en: not just to emphasize on Homeric warriors, but on the very idea of warriors.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是强调荷马式的勇士，而是强调勇士这一概念本身。

sentences.en: That's exactly as it is with the Vikings, right?
sentences.zh: 这和维京人完全一样，对吧？

sentences.en: It's all about multicultural trading links and, you know, rethinking gender roles.
sentences.zh: 全都是关于多元文化的贸易联系，还有，你知道的，对性别角色的重新思考。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And celebrating migration.
sentences.zh: 而且在赞美迁徙。

sentences.en: And actually, what everybody's itching to say is, what about the stuff about smashing people's heads in with axes?
sentences.zh: 其实，每个人心里最痒痒想说的是，用斧头把别人的脑袋砸碎是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Where's all that?
sentences.zh: 那些都去哪儿了？

sentences.en: That's the fun stuff.
sentences.zh: 那才是好玩的部分。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, most obviously the fact that you've got these enormous fortifications built out of colossal giant cyclopean boulders.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，最明显的证据就是那些由巨大的巨石筑成的宏伟防御工事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so there's a wonderful book on this whole process by a scholar called Cathy Gere about kind of the way that Mycenae has been understood.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一本关于整个过程的精彩著作，由一位名叫凯茜·杰尔的学者撰写，讲述了迈锡尼是如何被理解的。

sentences.en: And she quotes a very distinguished scholar who says that the citadels, you know,
sentences.zh: 她引用了一位非常杰出的学者的观点，他说这些城堡，你知道的，

sentences.en: Mycenae and other such cities served as symbols of the exalted status and the power of their rulers rather than as fortresses.
sentences.zh: 迈锡尼和其他此类城市与其说是要塞，不如说是其统治者崇高地位和权力的象征。

sentences.en: And that even though these fortresses are marked by cycles of destruction and rebuilding and then destruction again,
sentences.zh: 尽管这些要塞经历了毁灭与重建、再毁灭的循环，

sentences.en: that actually this is due to earthquakes and not to kind of violent conflict.
sentences.zh: 但实际上这是由于地震，而不是由于激烈的冲突。

sentences.en: So in a sense, it's standing the whole Schliemann-esque idea that he has found evidence for the Trojan War on its head.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这颠覆了施利曼关于他找到了特洛伊战争证据的整个观点。

sentences.en: There was no Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 根本没有特洛伊战争。

sentences.en: The Mycenaeans were not kind of brutal warlords.
sentences.zh: 迈锡尼人并不是什么残暴的军阀。

sentences.en: It was all international trading and bureaucracy and weaving and so on.
sentences.zh: 这全都是国际贸易、官僚体制和纺织等等。

sentences.en: But it has to be said that I think the pendulum on that has swung back pretty hard.
sentences.zh: 但必须承认，我认为这方面的天平已经相当猛烈地摆回去了。

sentences.en: That kind of 60s idea that ancient peoples are all, you know, all about beads and things.
sentences.zh: 那种六十年代的观点，认为古代人全都是，你知道的，只关心珠子之类的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're not building those big walls just for fun.
sentences.zh: 你总不能为了好玩去建那些大墙吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You're building them because there are some other people over the other hill who want to kill you.
sentences.zh: 你建它们是因为山那边还有些人想要你的命。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so Cathy Gere, again, she quotes another scholar responding to this idea that the marks of destruction in Mycenaean cities were caused by earthquakes.
sentences.zh: 所以凯茜·杰尔再次引用了另一位学者的观点，反驳迈锡尼城市中的毁灭痕迹是由地震造成的这一说法。

sentences.en: She said, yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 她说，得了吧。

sentences.en: The building of massive cyclopean walls is not a useful response to an earthquake.
sentences.zh: 修建庞大的巨石墙并不是应对地震的有效方法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Of course, I mean, you know, she's entirely true.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，你知道，她完全是对的。

sentences.en: And what has been happening, I think, over the past decades, I mean, it's not exactly saying that Schliemann was right,
sentences.zh: 我认为，在过去的几十年里发生的事情，并不是说施利曼完全正确，

sentences.en: that he'd found the Troy that was destroyed by the Greeks in the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 即他找到了在特洛伊战争中被希腊人毁灭的特洛伊。

sentences.en: But that it is all rooted in a much more solid foundations of historicity than perhaps people had thought about, you know, 40 or 50 years ago.
sentences.zh: 而是这一切都植根于比四五十年前人们想象的要坚实得多的历史基础之上。

sentences.en: And one of the key influences on this is that a whole load of texts from an empire to the east of Troy in what's now Turkey called the Hittite Empire.
sentences.zh: 其中一个关键影响是，从特洛伊以东一个帝国（现今土耳其境内，被称为赫梯帝国）出土了大量文献。

sentences.en: Loads of these have been found and they're being kind of translated.
sentences.zh: 其中许多文献已经被发现，并且正在被翻译。

sentences.en: You know, the translation is ongoing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，翻译工作仍在进行中。

sentences.en: And it kind of portrays a world of great power politics that actually does seem to kind of meld with the idea of there having been a Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 它描绘了一个大国政治的世界，这实际上似乎与曾经发生过特洛伊战争的观点相吻合。

sentences.en: And it does suggest that perhaps Troy is a kind of buffer state between the empires of the Hittites and the empires of the Akiwawa, which might be the Achaeans,
sentences.zh: 这确实表明，特洛伊可能曾是赫梯帝国与阿希瓦瓦帝国（可能是指亚该亚人）之间的一个缓冲国，

sentences.en: which is the name Homer gives to the Greeks in his epics.
sentences.zh: 亚该亚人是荷马史诗中对希腊人的称呼。

sentences.en: And that maybe that was what was going on.
sentences.zh: 也许当时发生的就是这种情况。

sentences.en: And I think also archaeology has demonstrated that the portrayal of Greek kingdoms in Homer does map on to the evidence from the Bronze Age.
sentences.zh: 我认为考古学也已经证明，荷马对希腊王国的描绘确实与青铜时代的证据相吻合。

sentences.en: You know, it does seem to be an authentic record of which cities were significant, which ones weren't.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这似乎是一份真实的记录，记录了哪些城市重要，哪些不重要。

sentences.en: And we know from the tablets that these kingdoms were ruled by, you know, a man called a Wanax.
sentences.zh: 我们从泥板中得知，这些王国由一个被称为“瓦纳克斯”（Wanax）的人统治。

sentences.en: And that's not so far from Homer's word, Anax.
sentences.zh: 这与荷马的词“安纳克斯”（Anax）相差不远。

sentences.en: So you can kind of see where the derivation of Agamemnon's title as Anax Andron, the ruler of men, that it might have come authentically from the Bronze Age.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出阿伽门农的头衔“Anax Andron”（人类的统治者）的词源，它可能真实地来源于青铜时代。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's the men.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是男人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What about the women?
sentences.zh: 那女人呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What about Helen?
sentences.zh: 海伦呢？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, the women at the core of our story, having taken into account Schliemann and also the developments in academic, thinking about all this.
sentences.zh: 因为，我是说，在考虑到施利曼以及学术界对这一切的思考进展之后，我们故事核心的女性——

sentences.en: Tom, where are we with Helen and with her sister, Clyde Zemnestra?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，关于海伦和她的姐姐克吕泰涅斯特拉，我们目前了解到什么程度了？

sentences.en: So by far the most readable and enjoyable study of how Helen herself might have been rooted in memories of how women in the Bronze Age, Bronze Age queens might have lived,
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，关于海伦本人如何扎根于青铜时代女性、青铜时代王后生活记忆的研究中，最可读、最令人愉快的，

sentences.en: is Bettany Hughes's book on Helen of Troy, which I mentioned in the first episode.
sentences.zh: 当属贝塔尼·休斯（Bettany Hughes）所著的《特洛伊的海伦》，我在第一集中提到过这本书。

sentences.en: And she kind of makes her case at the opening of her book.
sentences.zh: 她在书的开篇阐明了自己的观点。

sentences.en: Because Helen is such an alluring figure of fantasy, because she dazzles as she goes,
sentences.zh: 因为海伦是一个如此迷人的幻想人物，因为她光芒四射、光彩夺目，

sentences.en: she can make it hard to see the women of substance who walked through the Bronze Age palaces of the Eastern Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人很难注意到那些漫步于东地中海青铜时代宫殿中的有血有肉的女性。

sentences.en: But ongoing archaeological and historical projects demonstrate that these women were prominent and significant.
sentences.zh: 但正在进行的考古和历史项目表明，这些女性地位显赫、意义重大。

sentences.en: And I think she absolutely makes her case about that, you know, by going through the evidence and looking specifically for evidence of queens.
sentences.zh: 我认为她通过梳理证据并专门寻找王后的证据，绝对充分地证明了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, women like Helen and Clyde Zemnestra are not apparent in, say, the 5th century BC.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，像海伦和克吕泰涅斯特拉这样的女性在公元前5世纪并不明显。

sentences.en: That's the whole point of Aeschylus' play, that the age where monstrous women like Clyde Zemnestra could sway the destiny of a state.
sentences.zh: 这就是埃斯库罗斯戏剧的全部意义所在，那个像克吕泰涅斯特拉那样拥有左右国家命运之力的可怕女性的时代，

sentences.en: But, you know, that is long gone in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那已经是很久以前的过去了。

sentences.en: But if you look back to the evidence in the Bronze Age, I think you do find that queens did have a kind of elevated role.
sentences.zh: 但如果你回看青铜时代的证据，我认为你确实会发现王后们确实拥有某种崇高的地位。

sentences.en: So Bettany kind of adduces all kinds of evidence.
sentences.zh: 所以贝塔尼列举了各种证据。

sentences.en: So Bettany is making the case specifically for Helen.
sentences.zh: 因此，贝塔尼是在专门为海伦进行论证。

sentences.en: And I think she does adduce fascinating evidence for how the traditions that are told about Helen might have originated in kind of authentic Bronze Age practices.
sentences.zh: 我认为她确实列举了迷人的证据，证明围绕海伦流传的传统是如何起源于真实的青铜时代习俗的。

sentences.en: But just looking at it slightly broader before we zoom in on Helen, so looking at Mycenae, for instance, the home of Clyde Zemnestra,
sentences.zh: 但在我们将镜头聚焦于海伦之前，先稍微宏观地看一下，比如看看克吕泰涅斯特拉的故乡迈锡尼，

sentences.en: it is absolutely clear from the archaeology that women were present in the citadel.
sentences.zh: 从考古学上绝对可以清楚地看到，城堡中是有女性存在的。

sentences.en: And also that just as Clyde Zemnestra is portrayed in Homer and in Aeschylus, they lived in unsegregated ways.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如克吕泰涅斯特拉在荷马和埃斯库罗斯作品中所描绘的那样，她们的生活并没有被隔离。

sentences.en: So Agamemnon and Clyde Zemnestra could absolutely be imagined going into the bathroom together as Aeschylus portrays them.
sentences.zh: 所以完全可以想象，阿伽门农和克吕泰涅斯特拉会像埃斯库罗斯所描绘的那样一起走进浴室。

sentences.en: And we know that because their artifacts are found together and they're buried together, things like that.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为他们的随身物品是一起被发现的，而且他们也是被合葬在一起的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Well, there's one room in particular in Mycenae where there's evidence of weaving.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈锡尼有一个特定的房间有织布的痕迹。

sentences.en: So that is a marker of women, but there are also kind of arrowheads there.
sentences.zh: 所以那是女性的标志，但那里也有一些箭头。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that suggests a kind of mixing of male and female going on.
sentences.zh: 所以这表明当时存在一种男女交融的现象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And as you say, also there is no segregation in death.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，死后也没有性别隔离。

sentences.en: So these shaft graves excavated by Schliemann, there are female bodies as well as male bodies.
sentences.zh: 因此，由施利曼发掘的这些竖穴墓中，既有女性遗体，也有男性遗体。

sentences.en: Although the women don't have masks, they kind of have strips of gold diadems on their heads.
sentences.zh: 尽管女性没有面具，但她们的头上戴着金质头饰带。

sentences.en: And kind of broadening it out to look at kind of some of the things that you get in Homeric epic.
sentences.zh: 如果把视野放宽一点，来看看荷马史诗中出现的一些事物。

sentences.en: So the idea that the abduction of women might be a cause for war, there seems to be evidence for that in some of the Hittite tablets.
sentences.zh: 所以，绑架女性可能是引发战争的原因这一观点，在一些赫梯泥板中似乎有据可循。

sentences.en: There's definitely evidence for high-ranking women being used as kind of diplomatic tools or kind of trading chips.
sentences.zh: 绝对有证据表明，高地位的女性被用作某种外交工具或交易筹码。

sentences.en: You know, they're kind of commodities to be passed from great kingdom to great kingdom.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她们就像是从一个大王国传到另一个大王国的商品。

sentences.en: And if you think of the passage that I read about Clytemnestra weaving this kind of voluminous shroud that traps Agamemnon so he can then be butchered.
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下我读过的那段话，克吕泰涅斯特拉织造了一件庞大的寿衣，把阿伽门农困在其中，这样他就可以被屠杀。

sentences.en: He gets kind of hacked to death in the bath.
sentences.zh: 他在浴室里被乱刀砍死。

sentences.en: You also have Helen is described in the Iliad as kind of embroidering a great purple robe.
sentences.zh: 在《伊利亚特》中，海伦也被描述为在绣一件巨大的紫色长袍。

sentences.en: And of course, very famously, Penelope, the wife of Odysseus, while she's waiting for her husband to return,
sentences.zh: 当然，非常著名的还有奥德修斯的妻子珀涅洛佩，在她等待丈夫归来的期间，

sentences.en: she's weaving and then unpicking her cloth all the way to try and keep her suitors at bay.
sentences.zh: 她一边织布，一边又一路拆掉织物，以此来打发追求者。

sentences.en: And this image of great women at the head of weavers, of servant girls, this again,
sentences.zh: 这种伟大的女性带领着织女和女佣的形象，同样，

sentences.en: there's absolutely evidence for this in the tablets that have survived from the Bronze Age palaces like Mycenae.
sentences.zh: 在迈锡尼等青铜时代宫殿幸存下来的泥板中，绝对有这方面的证据。

sentences.en: And so Linear B, it's much more like Chinese or hieroglyphs.
sentences.zh: 所以，线性文字B更类似于中文或象形文字。

sentences.en: It's not an alphabet.
sentences.zh: 它不是字母文字。

sentences.en: The image for a woman is you have two dots for a breast, you have kind of arms sticking out, you have what's clearly a skirt and you have what seems to be a kind of curl of hair.
sentences.zh: 女性的图像是：两个点代表胸部，有伸出的手臂，有明显的裙子，似乎还有一个卷曲的头发。

sentences.en: So for a man, it's a straight line.
sentences.zh: 而对于男性，则是一条直线。

sentences.en: You know, he's had his hair cut.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他剪过头发。

sentences.en: For a woman, it's a kind of curve, like it's a braid or something.
sentences.zh: 对于女性，则是一个曲线，就像是辫子之类的东西。

sentences.en: And all of this seems to kind of gel with what you get in Homer, the portrayal of great women and their ranks of servants.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切似乎都与你在荷马作品中所看到的相吻合，即对伟大女性及其成群仆人的描绘。

sentences.en: Now, what about Helen herself?
sentences.zh: 那么，海伦本人呢？

sentences.en: So this is the evidence, among lots of other evidence, that Bettany uses for the memories of Helen being rooted in Bronze Age ideals of beauty.
sentences.zh: 这就是贝塔尼用来证明海伦的记忆扎根于青铜时代审美理想的证据，其中也包含许多其他证据。

sentences.en: So we talked about how Helen is described as xanthe.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论过海伦如何被描述为“xanthe”。

sentences.en: Golden head.
sentences.zh: 金发。

sentences.en: Golden head or red head, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许是金发或红发。

sentences.en: And Bettany points out that on the island of Thera, you know, the great volcanic eruption.
sentences.zh: 贝塔尼指出，在锡拉岛上，你知道，那场巨大的火山爆发。

sentences.en: Yeah, modern day Santorini.
sentences.zh: 对，即现代的圣托里尼。

sentences.en: That set a tsunami overwhelming Crete, which is one of the theories for where the story of Atlantis came from.
sentences.zh: 那场火山爆发引发了海啸，淹没了克里特岛，这是亚特兰蒂斯传说来源的理论之一。

sentences.en: And it buried these frescoes a bit like Pompeii.
sentences.zh: 它像庞贝古城一样掩埋了这些壁画。

sentences.en: And there are lots of portraits of aristocratic women on it.
sentences.zh: 上面有很多贵族女性的画像。

sentences.en: And most of them, you know, they have dark hair, but there are people with lighter hair.
sentences.zh: 她们大多数，你知道，都是深色头发，但也有浅色头发的人。

sentences.en: And she points out that there is one in particular who has red hair.
sentences.zh: 她指出，其中有一个人特别引人注目，她长着红发。

sentences.en: These are women close to the image of a deity and that this woman is closest to the deity.
sentences.zh: 这些是接近神明形象的女性，而这个女人离神明最近。

sentences.en: And most of the mortals don't wear a necklace.
sentences.zh: 大多数凡人都不戴项链。

sentences.en: The necklace seems to be a symbol for a god.
sentences.zh: 项链似乎是神的象征。

sentences.en: But this particular mortal, the one with the red hair, she is wearing a necklace.
sentences.zh: 但这个特殊的凡人，那个红发女子，她戴着项链。

sentences.en: So perhaps there's a kind of implication there that to have red or golden hair is somehow seen as a marker of kind of semi-divine status.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许暗示着，拥有红发或金发在某种程度上被视为半神地位的标志。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a fascinating theory.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个迷人的理论。

sentences.en: There is, we described how Helen is always described as being kind of white, like the shell of the egg from which she emerged.
sentences.zh: 我们描述过海伦总是被形容为白皙，就像她孵化时那枚蛋的蛋壳一样。

sentences.en: And lots of white lead oxide has been found, which seems to have been used as kind of cosmetics.
sentences.zh: 人们发现了大量白色氧化铅，它似乎曾被用作某种化妆品。

sentences.en: So to quote Bethany, the overall effect is mesmerizing.
sentences.zh: 用贝塔尼的话来引用，整体效果是迷人的。

sentences.en: Women made up in this way have great impact.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式化妆的女性具有巨大的冲击力。

sentences.en: They become walking effigies.
sentences.zh: 她们变成了行走的偶像。

sentences.en: Their faces take on the appearance of a mask.
sentences.zh: 她们的面容呈现出面具的模样。

sentences.en: Their painted bodies move from the natural to the supernatural.
sentences.zh: 她们涂脂抹粉的身体从自然走向了超自然。

sentences.en: So again, very, very potent.
sentences.zh: 所以同样地，非常、非常有感染力。

sentences.en: And I think that, I mean, obviously it's not conclusive, but it's interesting enough, I think, to satisfy the yearning that, oh no, I've always wanted it to be true.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这显然不是决定性的，但它足够有趣，足以满足人们内心的渴望：哦，不，我一直希望这是真的。

sentences.en: So what all that is suggesting is that the portrait of Helen, it's not saying that somebody called Helen existed.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些都表明，对海伦的描绘并不是在说一个叫海伦的人曾经存在过。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: But it's basically saying the portrait that you get of a golden haired princess, very powerful.
sentences.zh: 但它基本上是在说，你所看到的金发公主的形象，是非常强大的。

sentences.en: She lives in the world of servants and weavers.
sentences.zh: 她生活在仆人和织工的世界里。

sentences.en: She moves through the palace.
sentences.zh: 她在宫殿里穿行。

sentences.en: She's wearing white makeup to whiten her features.
sentences.zh: 她涂着白色的妆容来修饰面部特征。

sentences.en: Yeah, and she might be used as kind of a chip in international relations.
sentences.zh: 没错，她可能被当作国际关系中的一种筹码。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She might be sent away or there might be some breakdown in negotiations in which possession of her becomes a political controversy.
sentences.zh: 她可能会被送走，或者谈判可能会破裂，导致她的归属权成为一场政治争议。

sentences.en: And also she wears a necklace that suggests that she might end up occupying a position that has a hint of the divine about it.
sentences.zh: 而且她还戴着一条项链，暗示她最终可能会占据一个带有神圣色彩的位置。

sentences.en: And that's what Helen is ultimately representing.
sentences.zh: 而这正是海伦最终所代表的。

sentences.en: So when the story first begins, to its first listeners, because of course it's an oral tradition, isn't it, with these stories initially, to the first listeners,
sentences.zh: 所以当故事刚开始时，对于最初的听众来说——因为当然，这些故事最初是以口头传统形式流传的，不是吗？——对于最初的听众而言，

sentences.en: she would be an immediately recognizable figure as a Bronze Age queen.
sentences.zh: 她会是一个一眼就能辨认出的青铜时代王后形象。

sentences.en: I mean, the thing is, we haven't really done an episode on the historicity of the Trojan War generally.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，问题在于，我们其实还没有做过一期关于特洛伊战争总体历史真实性的节目。

sentences.en: But, I mean, there is no question that there are fragments of language and of authentic elements of the Bronze Age world preserved in Homer.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，毫无疑问，荷马史诗中保留了青铜时代世界的语言片段和真实元素。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think the idea that the portrayal of queens, so like Helen, like Clytemnestra, in Homer, that that preserves a memory that is true to the Bronze Age palaces,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，荷马对王后们的刻画——比如海伦，比如克吕泰涅斯特拉——这种刻画保留了忠于青铜时代宫殿的记忆，

sentences.en: I think is not beyond the bounds of possibility.
sentences.zh: 我认为并非完全不可能。

sentences.en: What about, as we move towards the end, what about this idea that, I guess, a lot of feminist critics have advanced?
sentences.zh: 那么，当我们走向尾声时，许多女性主义评论家提出的这种观点又如何呢？

sentences.en: I mean, there's this huge trend obviously now, isn't there, in fiction and literary fiction for rewriting the Greek myths and rewriting them, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在小说和文学小说界显然有一个巨大的趋势，那就是重写希腊神话，你知道的，

sentences.en: often women writers who are rewriting them from a female's perspective,
sentences.zh: 通常是由女性作家从女性的视角来重写，

sentences.en: maybe giving female characters more agency or talking about the sexual violence that they suffer and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 也许赋予女性角色更多的主动性，或者谈论她们遭受的性暴力以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Where do you think Helen and Clytemnestra stand?
sentences.zh: 你认为海伦和克吕泰涅斯特拉处于什么位置？

sentences.en: Because clearly for the Greeks who heard those stories, they were very unsettling figures.
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，对于听到这些故事的希腊人来说，她们是非常令人不安的人物。

sentences.en: And you could, of course, argue from our perspective that, you know, if you're a woman listening to that, presumably you're very conscious of the way in which they are objectified,
sentences.zh: 当然，你也可以从我们的角度争辩说，如果你是一个听这些故事的女性，大概你会非常清楚她们被客体化的方式，

sentences.en: their sexuality is seen as something dangerous and deadly,
sentences.zh: 她们的性被视为某种危险和致命的东西，

sentences.en: and that that is the beginning of a tradition that runs right through Western literature and is a kind of baleful tradition.
sentences.zh: 而这正是贯穿整个西方文学的某种不祥传统的开端。

sentences.en: Well, I think that, I mean, Clytemnestra certainly has agency.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为，克吕泰涅斯特拉确实拥有主动权。

sentences.en: I mean, she butchers her husband in the bath.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她在浴室里屠宰了自己的丈夫。

sentences.en: And Helen also has agency.
sentences.zh: 海伦也拥有主动权。

sentences.en: And actually, the post-classical tradition of casting her as a victim of rape denies her the agency that she has if she decides she's fed up with Menelaus.
sentences.zh: 事实上，后古典时代将她塑造成强奸受害者的传统，剥夺了她本应拥有的主动权——如果她决定自己受够了墨涅拉俄斯的话。

sentences.en: She's going to take her gold and treasure and go off and, you know, hitch up with Paris.
sentences.zh: 她打算带上她的黄金和宝藏，然后离开，你知道的，去和帕里斯在一起。

sentences.en: I think that Clytemnestra is clearly seen as a monstrous and terrifying figure, but she completely dominates Aeschylus' tragedy.
sentences.zh: 我认为克吕泰涅斯特拉显然被视为一个怪异而可怕的人物，但她完全主导了埃斯库罗斯的悲剧。

sentences.en: I mean, she is by far the most powerful figure within it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她是其中当之无愧的最强人物。

sentences.en: And you could say that that is an expression of the kind of the nightmares of Aeschylus' audience, because in Athens, you know, women don't have any form of political power.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，那是埃斯库罗斯观众内心某种噩梦的表达，因为在雅典，你知道的，女性没有任何形式的政治权力。

sentences.en: But they do have a role as mediators between the state of Athens and the gods.
sentences.zh: 但她们确实扮演着雅典城邦与神灵之间调解人的角色。

sentences.en: And Clytemnestra might serve as a kind of warning of what happens if women ignore that role.
sentences.zh: 而克吕泰涅斯特拉或许可以作为一个警示，告诫人们如果女性忽视这一角色会发生什么。

sentences.en: I mean, Greek tragedy is full of very, very powerful women.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，希腊悲剧中充满了非常非常强大的女性。

sentences.en: And it does seem that the power of those women is a kind of expression of anxieties that are kind of inherent.
sentences.zh: 而且这些女性的力量似乎正是某种固有焦虑的表达。

sentences.en: These are women who've got above themselves.
sentences.zh: 这些都是些自视甚高、越界行事的女性。

sentences.en: Is that basically what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是你想表达的吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it's above themselves.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是越界行事。

sentences.en: It's the notion that the proper order of things, as the Athenians of the 5th century BC understand them, that it threatens catastrophe and disaster.
sentences.zh: 这是这样一种观念：正如公元前5世纪的雅典人所理解的那样，如果违背了事物的正确秩序，就会招致灾难和毁灭。

sentences.en: And that's why the cycle of revenge and bloodshed that Clytemnestra is involved in, the fact that it is settled by the virgin figure of Athena, who is, of course, herself female,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么克吕泰涅斯特拉卷入的那场复仇与流血的循环，最终是由处女雅典娜来解决的——当然，雅典娜本身也是女性，

sentences.en: but in the context of Athens is so important.
sentences.zh: 但在雅典的语境下，她是如此重要。

sentences.en: Because Athena is indisputably powerful, but, you know, she's not killing people and overthrowing them, although traditionally she always has done.
sentences.zh: 因为雅典娜无可争议地强大，但是，你知道的，她并没有杀人或推翻政权，尽管传统上她一直都在这样做。

sentences.en: But it's a very kind of specific vision of the role that women and men should properly play.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种非常具体的愿景，关于女性和男性本应扮演的角色。

sentences.en: And I think with Helen, I mean, she's incredibly powerful.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为海伦也是如此，我的意思是，她极其强大。

sentences.en: She is terrifying.
sentences.zh: 她令人畏惧。

sentences.en: And it's the quality of all the heroes in Greek myth that they are powerful.
sentences.zh: 希腊神话中所有英雄的共同特质就是他们都很强大。

sentences.en: And Socrates, I think, you know, is putting his finger on something very significant about those myths when he says that beauty is more powerful than strength.
sentences.zh: 我认为苏格拉底说“美比力量更强大”时，他精准地指出了这些神话中非常重要的一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think he's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想他是对的。

sentences.en: So thank you for that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: That was absolutely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这真的太引人入胜了。

sentences.en: Loads of things that we can come back to maybe in the rest of this history.
sentences.zh: 还有很多事情我们可以在接下来的历史探讨中重新涉足。

sentences.en: So the Trojan War, the story of Schliemann, Greek gods and Greek heroes more generally.
sentences.zh: 比如特洛伊战争、施里曼的故事，以及更广泛的希腊神话和希腊英雄。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell, we will see you next week.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅炸弹，我们下周见。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
